title: CS2 World Bundle lane-prefab catalogue (laneprefabs.json, contract section 5B v2)
description: A flat object keyed by lane-prefab name: the STRAIGHT part meshes a drawing lane assembles along its curve, shipped once. lanemeshes.jsonl carries the per-lane bend parameters that reference these entries; the bend algorithm is normative in contract section 5B. This is what makes the layer dedupe-by-prefab (section 6): the reference city draws 33,500 lanes from 94 part meshes.

assetId.description: Filesystem-safe: ASCII alphanumerics, dot, underscore and hyphen; must start with an alphanumeric.

entry.description: One lane prefab that draws geometry. A lane prefab with no parts is not written at all.

category.description: From CS2's UtilityTypes. 'cable' and 'pipe' are utility runs, 'fence' is fences and hedge rows, 'lane' is everything drawn along a road lane (wear tint, markings).

hanging.description: UtilityLaneData.m_Hanging — the prefab-level sag factor. 0 when the prefab never sags. The per-lane drop at each end is lanemeshes.jsonl's own 'hang'; this is the h in the cubic (d0, (d0+h*L)*2/3, (d1+h*L)*2/3, d1).

parts.description: The prefab's sub-meshes, in the order lanemeshes.jsonl's 'parts' indices refer to. A lane draws the subset its own record names, not all of them.

part.description: One straight part mesh plus how it is laid along the curve.

assetId.description: Resolves to <layers.laneMeshes><assetId>.glb, standard mesh frame (section 2.2 / 6), materials joining materials.json as everywhere else.

pos.description: Part offset within the prefab, bundle mesh frame (section 2.2).

rot.description: Part rotation within the prefab as a unit quaternion [x, y, z, w].

inverted.description: MeshFlags.Invert — the bend runs the curve backwards for this part.

tilingCount.description: MeshData.m_TilingCount. Feeds the game's GetTileCount, which the consumer must port verbatim rather than dividing lengths: N = L / max(1, size.z) quantised through the clip window, and 0 means the part draws nothing (contract section 5B).

geometryTiling.description: MeshFlags.Tiling — true means the part really repeats along the curve, false means one instance stretched across it.

boundsMin.description: Authored bounds, low corner. The z span (boundsMax[2] - boundsMin[2]) is the tile length the tile count is measured in.

decal.description: The game projects this part onto the ground rather than drawing it as standing geometry — road markings and wear tint. Emitted only when true. A consumer drapes these onto its terrain and lifts them off it by the section 8b ladder; it must never generate collision from one.

decalRole.description: Which kind of ground projection this is (2026-08-09, audit #40). 'marking' is painted line work, 'wear' is the tinted asphalt/gravel surface under it — they take different lifts on the drape ladder. The producer classifies from the part material's tint alpha (wear surfaces carry tint.a < 1, markings carry no tint) and omits the key when no material resolves. An ABSENT key means unknown, not either class: do not fall back to string-matching the assetId, which is what this key replaced because it fails on mods.
